question: Of the dip events whose underlying never regained its pre-dip high before the position was closed, how many saw the underlying return to the ENTRY price within 365 days after exit?
why_it_matters: It separates two failure modes that look identical in the P&L: a dip that genuinely did not come back (the moat cracked), and a dip that did come back after the call had already expired (the clock, not the thesis, was wrong).
recovery_level_caveat: the entry price is an easier level to reach than the pre-dip trailing high, which was not retained per trade, so the share is an UPPER bound on the fraction of dips rescued by a longer horizon
inference_caveat: recovery within a year of exit does not imply a longer-dated call would have profited: a longer hold pays more theta. The probe establishes that the clock missed the recovery, not that removing the clock would have made money.
produced_by: qc/option_clock_probe_qc.py in the original study, executed on the data vendor's research platform (daily equity history for 282 names/dates)

What IS checked locally, by run.py, is the denominator: deduplicating the never-recovered trades in universe_trades.parquet to unique (ticker, entry_date) dip events must yield exactly n_events, which ties this recovered number to this exact trade record.
